question.problem: A laboratory test for a particular disease is conducted on some patients. Of the tested patients, $95%$ of those infected and $4%$ of those not infected tested positive for the disease. Only $10%$ of the entire population is infected with the disease. What is the probability that a randomly chosen patient that tested positive is infected? Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Let $D$ be the event that a randomly chosen patient is infected with the disease, and let $T$ be the event they tested positive. Then, we require $P(D|T),$ which we can compute using Bayes' theorem.

$$
P(D|T)=\frac{P(T|D)P(D)}{P(T)}=\frac{P(T|D)P(D)}{P(T|D)P(D)+P(T|{D}^{′})P({D}^{′})}
$$

From the problem statement, we have the following:

- Since the probability of an infected person testing positive is $95%,$ and the probability of a non-infected person testing positive is $4%,$ we have

$$
P(T|D)=0.95,\,P(T|{D}^{′})=0.04.
$$

- Since only $10%$ of the population has the disease, we have

$$
P(D)=0.1,\,P({D}^{′})=1-0.1=0.9.
$$

Therefore, using Bayes' theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D|T) & =\frac{P(T|D)P(D)}{P(T|D)P(D)+P(T|{D}^{′})P({D}^{′})} \\  & =\frac{(0.95)(0.1)}{(0.95)(0.1)+(0.04)(0.9)} \\  & ≈0.73\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
